# Glossary

Every mechanic word used anywhere in the book is defined here, once, from the
reader's question rather than the mechanism. Pages link to it with
`[[term]]`. An entry that can only be written in mechanism words marks a term
that does not belong in Part I.

## A

### account

A mailbox connected to downcroc that can send mail and, when enabled, watch
for replies and bounces. An account has a state and credentials, send
transports/bindings, and its own policy, and it is the sender jobs run from.

More: [account](../part-ii/07-account/account.md), [mailboxes](../part-i/04-mailboxes/one-mailbox.md)

See also: [[provider]], [[transport]], [[needs-reauth]], [[vault]]

### allowance

How many sends one mailbox may make per day. When a mailbox spends its
allowance, it does not error; it waits until your local midnight and starts
again. Give two mailboxes different allowances and the daemon spreads work
between them by itself.

More: [mailboxes](../part-ii/07-account/account.md), [sending](../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md)

### approval

The review gate on a batch. A batch can wait awaiting approval until you
approve a sample or approve all to release messages for sending, or cancel it.
Approval controls when work is allowed to go out, separate from pausing.

More: [approve and cancel](../part-ii/08-batch/approve.md), [review](../part-ii/13-review/review.md), [submit](../part-ii/08-batch/submit.md)

See also: [[batch]], [[job]]

## B

### batch

A group of jobs created together from one file or one campaign. The batch is
how you see and steer work as a group: approve it, pause it, read its totals.

More: [batches](../part-ii/08-batch/inspect.md), [approve](../part-ii/08-batch/approve.md)

See also: [[job]]

## C

### campaign

The input you prepare and submit to send mail: its messages, routing and
options, and any follow-up steps. A campaign is read from a file (JSON or CSV
with a template), checked and previewed, and when submitted becomes a
[[batch]] of jobs.

More: [prepare](../part-ii/08-batch/prepare.md), [submit](../part-ii/08-batch/submit.md), [send](../part-ii/12-send/send.md)

See also: [[batch]], [[job]]

### code

The one-word reason a send failed, as the failed screen shows it. Every code
has a plain meaning; the complete list lives in the
[failed command chapter](../part-ii/10-failed/failed.md).

See also: [[failed]]

## D

### daemon

The background process that owns downcroc’s state and does the work: sending,
watching, syncing, and serving the local API. The CLI talks to the daemon; when
it is not running, nothing moves. Starting it does not unlock the [[vault]].

More: [service](../part-ii/01-service/service.md), [serve](../part-ii/01-service/serve.md), [status](../part-ii/02-status/status.md)

See also: [[vault]]

## F

### failed

A send that could not be delivered, with the reason recorded. A failed job is
kept, not thrown away, and it will try again on its own within the retry
rules unless the reason says the mailbox or the address made that pointless.

More: [the failed command](../part-ii/10-failed/failed.md), [why things fail](32-failures.md)

See also: [[job]], [[code]]

### follow-up

A follow-up is a message planned to go out after an earlier one, as a reply in the same [[thread]]. It waits for a set time and sends only when its condition is still true (for example when the person has not replied, depending on `when` and stop/suppression rules).

Follow-ups belong to a [[batch]] and are sent from the mailbox that sent the original message. A sequence is made of named follow-up steps, defined in a campaign file or added later as follow-up declarations.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)
- [../part-i/05-follow-ups/what-is-a-follow-up.md](../part-i/05-follow-ups/what-is-a-follow-up.md)

### follow-up declaration

A follow-up declaration defines a follow-up step for an existing campaign [[batch]] outside the original campaign file (using `batch followups declare` / related commands). Declarations can be **shared** (one template/patch applied per recipient with optional overrides) or **payload-backed** (explicit per-recipient messages with a schedule).

Declarations are versioned, can be declared before they run, removed before send, or retired to stop further planning while keeping history, subject to state and conflict rules.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)
- [../part-i/05-follow-ups/change-a-sequence.md](../part-i/05-follow-ups/change-a-sequence.md)

### follow-up override

A follow-up override customizes what a particular recipient receives for a named follow-up step. In a campaign JSON, overrides live under a message’s `followups` object keyed by step key (and may set `subject`, `text`, `html`, or `skip`). In a shared declaration, overrides are provided in the declaration’s `overrides` object keyed by parent message key.

Overrides must refer to known step/message keys as applicable.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)

### follow-up step

A follow-up step is a single planned follow-up in a sequence: it has a key, a wait (`after_days`), a condition (`when`, such as `no_reply` or `always`), the message content to send, and whether it requires approval.

Steps can be defined up front in a campaign’s `followups` list or added later as a follow-up declaration on a [[batch]]. Each step is identified by its key within that sequence/parent context.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)
- [../part-i/05-follow-ups/the-shape-of-a-sequence.md](../part-i/05-follow-ups/the-shape-of-a-sequence.md)

## H

### hold

A pause that prevents work from being dispatched while in effect, without
cancelling or deleting it. Holds can apply at the service, account, batch, or
job level; work proceeds again once the relevant holds are released and it is
otherwise eligible.

More: [batch holds](../part-ii/08-batch/holds.md), [service](../part-ii/01-service/service.md), [job](../part-ii/09-job/job.md)

See also: [[batch]], [[job]], [[queued]]

## I

### interpreter links

The small links named `python`, `python3`, and `pythonX.Y` inside the [[venv]] `bin` directory. They point at the Python interpreter that runs downcroc. When a system upgrade removes that interpreter, the links dangle or loop and downcroc will not start. [[repair]] points them at a Python that exists.

More: [repair](../part-ii/26-repair/repair.md)

See also: [[venv]], [[managed-install]], [[repair]]

## J

### jitter

Jitter is the pause downcroc waits between sending messages from a mailbox. By
spacing sends out instead of firing them back to back, it keeps the pace
steady and more like the rhythm of a person writing mail.

A mailbox's send policy sets a minimum and maximum gap, and downcroc chooses a
wait in that range between sends.

More:
- [../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md](../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md)

### job

One email that downcroc has been asked to send, together with everything it
needs: the recipient, the subject, the body, and the record of what happened
when it tried. A job is the unit you create, watch, and cancel. It exists
before it is sent and after, so the history is always readable.

More: [jobs](../part-ii/09-job/job.md)

See also: [[queued]], [[sent]], [[failed]], [[batch]]

## M

### managed install

An install that the supported install scripts set up. It has a launcher on your PATH and a [[venv]] under the application data directory. Commands like `update`, `uninstall`, and [[repair]] work with a managed install. If you made your own environment from a checkout, downcroc will not treat it as managed.

More: [update](../part-ii/24-update/update.md), [uninstall](../part-ii/25-uninstall/uninstall.md)

See also: [[venv]], [[repair]]

### max_in_flight

Max in flight is the number of sends a mailbox may have underway at the same
time. Keeping this low spaces work out; raising it allows more sends to run in
parallel for that mailbox, within the limits of how sending is configured.

More:
- [../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md](../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md)

## N

### needs-reauth

A mailbox that downcroc can no longer sign in to with the credential it has.
The address and your messages are still there, but the permission to send has
expired or been taken away. Nothing sends from it until you connect it again.

More: [broken mailboxes](../part-ii/07-account/account.md), [connecting Gmail](../part-i/01-starting/gmail.md)

See also: [[vault]], [[job]]

## P

### payload declaration

A payload declaration is a kind of [[follow-up declaration]] whose JSON provides a `followup` schedule block and a `messages` list (or an array/document form accepted by the parser) with one message per parent recipient. Each recipient gets the explicitly provided content for that step.

Payload declarations must cover the parent recipients (no gaps) without naming extras, and have stricter constraints than campaign messages (for example no attachments and no template variables in declaration payload messages).

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)

### provider

A declaration of how to talk to a mail service: its hosts and ports, auth
kind, capabilities (such as IMAP/SMTP or API), and any imported OAuth client
references. Accounts are created from providers.

More: [provider](../part-ii/06-provider/provider.md)

See also: [[account]], [[transport]]

## Q

### queued

Written down and waiting. A queued job has everything it needs; it is not
sending yet, either because you have not told it to or because its turn has
not come. Nothing is wrong with a queued job.

More: [job states](33-states.md)

See also: [[job]], [[sent]]

## R

### repair

The command that fixes a [[managed-install]] after a Python upgrade. It checks the [[interpreter-links]] in the [[venv]], points them at a Python that exists, and checks that downcroc is still in [[site-packages]].

More: [repair](../part-ii/26-repair/repair.md)

See also: [[managed-install]], [[venv]], [[interpreter-links]], [[site-packages]]

## S

### sending_window

A sending window is the span of local hours during which downcroc may send
mail from a mailbox. Outside that window, work waits until sending is allowed
again.

You can use a window to keep mail going out at sensible times of day rather
than around the clock.

More:
- [../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md](../part-ii/11-sending/sending.md)

### sent

The receiving mail server accepted the message. Accepted is the honest word:
it does not promise a human read it, and it does not promise delivery to the
inbox, only that the server took it.

More: [job states](33-states.md)

See also: [[job]], [[queued]]

### shared declaration

A shared declaration is a kind of [[follow-up declaration]] whose JSON defines the step schedule/condition and shared content (`text`/`html`, optional `subject`, `require_approval`) plus optional `overrides` keyed by parent message key. downcroc applies that shared content to eligible recipients, using any override for a specific recipient.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)

### site-packages

The folder inside the [[venv]] where Python keeps installed packages. If it is empty, the interpreter starts but cannot import downcroc. [[repair]] reports this as `needs_reinstall`, and `downcroc update --force` fixes it.

See also: [[venv]], [[repair]]

### suppressed

A recipient (or follow-up) withheld from further sending for a batch because a
rule or signal says not to contact them — for example after a reply or bounce,
or due to suppression/stop conditions. Suppressed work is recorded, not sent.

More: [inspect](../part-ii/08-batch/inspect.md), [followups](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)

See also: [[batch]], [[job]], [[follow_up]]

## T

### template

A template is a reusable message you can apply to many people. It holds the
subject and the body of the message, and it can include placeholders such as
`{{name}}` that downcroc fills in from the data for each recipient.

Templates are often paired with a CSV file, where each row supplies the values
that make the message personal.

More:
- [../part-ii/21-template.md](../part-ii/21-template.md)

### thread

A thread is a single conversation made of messages that reply to one another.
When messages share a thread, the people reading them see them grouped
together as one exchange instead of as separate, unrelated notes.

In downcroc, a follow-up is sent as a reply on the same thread as the original
message to that person.

More:
- [../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md](../part-ii/08-batch/followups.md)

### transport

A concrete send path for an account, such as SMTP or the Gmail API. A
transport/binding has its own health, priority, limits, and credentials, and
determines how messages are delivered from that account.

More: [account](../part-ii/07-account/account.md), [provider](../part-ii/06-provider/provider.md), [doctor](../part-ii/16-doctor/doctor.md)

See also: [[account]], [[provider]]

## V

### vault

The encrypted store that holds your mailboxes' credentials. It is locked when
the daemon is not running, unlocked while it works, and locked again on a
clean stop. A locked vault is normal; nothing sends until it is unlocked.

More: [vault commands](../part-ii/04-vault/vault.md)

### venv

A private Python environment kept inside your [[managed-install]]. It holds the packages downcroc needs, so a system Python upgrade does not change them. The [[interpreter-links]] inside it are what the launcher uses to start downcroc.

More: [repair](../part-ii/26-repair/repair.md)

See also: [[managed-install]], [[interpreter-links]], [[site-packages]], [[repair]]
